data.title: Water levels still rising in many flooded provinces
data.description: Floodwater levels continue to rise in almost half of the 27 inundated provinces, the Disaster Prevention and Mitigation Department said on Monday, as a new warning was issued for people living downstream from the Mae Klong River Dam in Kanchanaburi.

data.title: Jet ski 'drifter' surfing Bangkok flood arrested, fined
data.description: A man who rode a jet ski through Bangkok floodwaters, deliberately making waves along submerged Phetchaburi Road on Sunday evening, was later arrested and charged with causing a public nuisance.

data.title: Soldiers help clear baggage backlog at airport amid flooding
data.description: Soldiers were deployed to speed up the handling of gridlocked luggage at Suvarnabhumi Airport on Monday after city-wide flooding prevented many ground staff reporting for work, causing hours-long flight delays over the weekend.

data.title: Govt seeks special employee holiday for flood-hit businesses
data.description: The Department of Labour Protection and Welfare (DLPW) is asking businesses in Bangkok, Nonthaburi, Pathum Thani and Samut Prakan to declare Sept 28 and 29 as special holidays for employees facing the chaotic flooding in Bangkok.

data.title: Jet ski 'drifter' surfing Bangkok flood faces charges
data.description: A man who rode a jet ski through Bangkok floodwaters, deliberately making waves along submerged Phetchaburi Road on Sunday evening, was later arrested and charged with causing a public nuisance.

data.title: Eastern rail track partially reopens, airport link unaffected
data.description: Some train services resumed on the eastern line on Monday morning, but trains were still unable to reach flooded central Bangkok.

data.title: 700,000 suffering under Bangkok floods
data.description: Severe flooding in Bangkok was affecting about 329,000 families, about 700,000 people, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration said on Monday.

data.title: City Hall reports flooding on several streets
data.description: The Bangkok Metropolitan Administration reported flood levels from 16 centimetres to 47cm deep on several streets on Monday morning.

data.title: Food supplies 'still secure'
data.description: The government has warned consumers against panic buying and businesses against hoarding or price gouging as floods disrupt transport.

data.title: Govt moves to streamline provincial bureaucracy
data.description: The number of civil servants in provincial administration will be gradually reduced, with no new positions created from now on, Deputy Prime Minister Pakorn Nilprapunt said on Sunday.

data.title: Thousands stranded by rising waters
data.description: Bangkok is stepping up safety measures in flooded communities after a 58-year-old woman was electrocuted, with thousands stranded amid dangerously high water.

data.title: Floods force extra holiday
data.description: The cabinet has declared Monday and Tuesday special public holidays in Bangkok and three neighbouring provinces to ease travel disruption and protect the public amid widespread flooding.

data.title: Support pours in for brothers forced to scavenge for food
data.description: The sight of two brothers searching rubbish bins for food at night in Bang Bua Thong, Nonthaburi, has prompted an outpouring of support after their story went viral.

data.title: City's main airport, THAI to work on flight delays
data.description: Suvarnabhumi Airport is working with Thai Airways (THAI) to resolve flight and baggage delays caused by flooding-related shortages of ground-handling staff.

data.title: Sondhi campaign off to slow start
data.description: Sondhi Limthongkul has returned to the political stage, but his latest mobilisation has yet to generate the mass response associated with his earlier campaigns.

data.title: Cabinet declares Sept 28-29 official government holidays in light of flooding
data.description: The Cabinet has approved Sept 28 and 29 as official government holidays in Bangkok and three of its neighbouring provinces to help mitigate the impact from flooding and facilitate travel for residents, according to Deputy Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Watcharapol Khaokham.

data.title: Thai police cooperating with Korean content protection
data.description: Thailand's police force has signed an agreement of cooperation with South Korea on suppressing the copyright violation of South Korean video content.

data.title: Flood disaster zones in Nonthaburi, more rain forecast
data.description: Nonthaburi declared Muang and Pak Kret districts flood disaster zones on Sunday after days of rain and rising river levels sent water pouring through residents' homes.

data.title: Cabinet declares Sept 28-29 special public holidays in light of flooding
data.description: The Cabinet has approved Sept 28 and 29 as special public holidays in Bangkok and three of its neighbouring provinces to help mitigate the impact from flooding and facilitate travel for residents, according to Deputy Agriculture and Cooperatives Minister Watcharapol Khaokham.

data.title: Luggage chaos, flight delays at Suvarnabhumi airport
data.description: Passengers arriving at Suvarnabhumi airport have been forced to wait five or six hours for their baggage and numerous flights have been delayed since Saturday because off problems with Thai Airways’ ground operations.

data.title: Nida Poll: Opposition leader and his party most popular
data.description: An opinion survey found most respondents liked the opposition-core People's Party (PP) and its leader over Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and his Bhumjaithai Party (BJT).

data.title: Thousands stranded, Lat Krabang evacuates flooded residents
data.description: Rescuers rushed to evacuate bedridden patients, elderly residents and other vulnerable people from a flood-stricken housing estate in Bangkok's Lat Krabang district on Sunday, with floodwaters neck-high in some places.

data.title: AGT winner Nene Royal arrives back in Phuket
data.description: PHUKET - America's Got Talent 2026 winner Nene Royal arrived back home on this southern tourist island on Sunday morning to a warm welcome and a planned evening parade.

data.title: Schoolboy hailed for clearing rubbish from flooded city street
data.description: Amid heavy flooding in Bangkok, a schoolboy's simple act of civic-mindedness has drawn widespread praise online after he was filmed wading through murky water to collect floating rubbish before it could clog the drains.

data.title: Heavy flooding continues in eastern Bangkok
data.description: Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt said heavy flooding continued in eastern districts of Bangkok, where most main canals remained full on Sunday.

data.title: More rain in Central Plains, will ease off in Bangkok
data.description: It will rain heavily in the western part of the Central Plains while rain will continue and then start to decline in Greater Bangkok and the East on Sunday, according to the Meteorological Department.

data.title: Heavy flooding remains in eastern Bangkok
data.description: Bangkok governor Chadchart Sittipunt said heavy flooding continued in eastern districts of Bangkok as most main canals remained full on Sunday.

data.title: Heavy rain continues in Central Plains: weathermen
data.description: It will rain heavily in the western part of the Central Plains while rain will continue and start to decline in Greater Bangkok and the East on Sunday, according to the Meteorological Department.

data.title: Seaplane project studied
data.description: SATUN: Transport Ministry is assessing the feasibility of seaplane operations on Koh Lipe, focusing on safety and environmental impacts.

data.title: Unlicensed hotels closed
data.description: PHUKET: Five hotels in the province have been ordered to suspend operations temporarily after authorities found that they failed to obtain licences and meet improvement requirements.

data.title: Govt defends solar sector as China supplies 99.3% of imports
data.description: The government has defended the domestic solar industry after figures showed China supplied 99.3% of solar-panel imports in the first seven months of 2026.

data.title: CP firm to run Airport Rail Link until January under same rules
data.description: The State Railway of Thailand and Asia Era One, a CP Group company, have agreed that the private firm will keep running the Airport Rail Link for four more months.

data.title: Klatham keeps options open
data.description: The Klatham Party has caused a stir by going against the opposition whip's position and voting in support of the 2027 budget bill.

data.title: 10,000 troops sent to flood-hit provinces
data.description: More than 10,000 troops and 1,000 vehicles have been deployed nationwide to help people hit by heavy rain and flooding.

data.title: City storms likely to ease this week
data.description: Rainfall in Bangkok and parts of central and eastern Thailand is expected to ease from Monday, although flood-prone areas remain under watch.

data.title: Ekniti defends co-pay extension
data.description: The extension of the Thais Help Thais Plus co-payment scheme is a response to the ongoing energy crisis, not a populist policy, Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas said.
